rule: Shared cross-runtime behavior has one authority: runtime-core (Rust). Other languages consume bindings. Intentional mirrors require an entry here AND a parity contract for their kind: differentiable_mirror/behavioral_mirror/transitional_mirror must name real executable parity checks; diagnostic/experimental must declare 'none' parity with a reason. Each mirror MUST declare a `why_outside_rust` capability referencing the top-level capabilities block (ADR 0001, 2026-08-29 amendment).

kinds.differentiable_mirror: Differentiable surrogate of Rust-owned math (training gradients flow through it). Real parity checks REQUIRED.
kinds.behavioral_mirror: Non-differentiable behavioral reimplementation. Real parity checks REQUIRED.
kinds.transitional_mirror: Behavioral mirror on a tracked sunset path; same parity contract as behavioral_mirror PLUS a required `sunset` field naming the follow-up ADR/issue that removes it.
kinds.diagnostic: Offline/diagnostic tool, never consumed by training, runtime, or the model. Parity 'none' with reason.
kinds.experimental: Not wired into training or runtime; must not be promoted without a real parity check. Parity 'none' with reason.

typescript.description: TypeScript owns the browser surface. Files outside runtime-core/ may legitimately contain: browser APIs, UI, rendering, binding adapters that wrap wasm-orbit / onnxruntime-web, and model/metadata IO. Anything else (product semantics, shared constants, domain-state types) must live in Rust.

python.description: Python owns training and offline tooling. Files outside runtime-core/ may legitimately contain: training/optimization, autograd (including differentiable mirrors when differentiation prevents direct Rust calls), experiment orchestration, and offline diagnostics never consumed by the model. Anything else (feature semantics, cadence, observation packing, model I/O ordering, Map geometry, Physics, control semantics) must live in Rust.

mirrors.reason: Differentiable PyTorch surrogates so gradients flow during training. The Rust bindings are non-differentiable; the oracle path (orbit_controller_oracle_sequence / _ContourStep) defers the per-frame contour step to the Rust binding and only the backward pass is a surrogate.

Independent NumPy formula oracle used only by preflight to detect drift against Rust-generated feature vectors. Production and training extraction call runtime_core.FeatureExtractor through runtime_core_helpers; dataset-wide normalization aggregation remains Python-owned there and does not recompute feature semantics.
parity: none (diagnostic-only; scripts/preflight_parity.py check (g) compares this oracle with Rust-generated golden vectors)

mirrors.reason: Test-only mock substituted under vitest (globalThis.__vitest) so frontend unit tests run without loading the wasm binary. Never imported in production code.

Training-time CPU Julia renderer for loss-facing visual metrics (render_julia_set). Rendering-scoped, not controller/feature authority; the distance/proximity metrics delegate to runtime_core.sample_distance_field_py.
GPU (ModernGL) Julia renderer for training-time visual metrics with CPU fallback. Rendering-scoped; optional (--no-gpu-rendering bypasses it).
Diagnostic-only plotting: cardioid/bulb outlines and an escape-time background grid for the c-trace figure. Never consumed by training, runtime, or the model.
parity: none (diagnostic-only; excluded from runtime paths by review)

mirrors.reason: EXPERIMENTAL live-performance controller (only referenced by backend/examples/live_controller_demo.py). Computes a separate analysis vocabulary (mel bands, tonalness, onset rate) that is NOT the canonical features/2 contract. Not wired into training or the runtime; must not become one without either delegating to runtime_core.FeatureExtractor or registering a real parity check.
parity: none (experimental; see reason â€” do not promote without parity)
